solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Footwear worn by socially acceptable form of 10

indicators.note: footwear is worn by the wearer, so the footwear word wraps round the letter for socially acceptable

parts.note: hose are stockings or tights, a kind of footwear
U is the old label for upper-class, socially acceptable usage

explanation.surface: Some shoes are worn by a socially acceptable sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is MUSIC, so 'form of 10' asks for a musical genre.
explanation.definitionFit: House is a genre of electronic dance music, so it is a form of music.

clue.text: Physically restrains workers, absorbing blow

indicators.note: absorbing means taking something in, so the workers word holds the blow word inside

parts.note: hands are manual workers
a cuff is a light blow with the hand

explanation.surface: Labourers restrain someone physically while soaking up a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Handcuffs as a verb means to shackle someone's wrists, restraining them bodily.

clue.text: Take over American university vacant readership

indicators.note: vacant means emptied of contents, so only the outer letters of readership remain

explanation.surface: An American university seizes control of a readership that has gone empty.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to seize power or a position wrongfully, taking it over.

clue.text: Choose right, love, and finish with silver!

parts.note: to elect is to choose
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to pick the right partner and end up with a silver medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Electro is short for electroplate, coating an object with a silver finish by electrolysis.

clue.text: The purging effect of desperate act is rash

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild, frantic behaviour, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A rash act committed in desperation proves to have a cleansing effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Catharsis is emotional release, a purging of pent-up feelings, from the Greek for cleansing.

clue.text: Mentioning mainly Liverpool, for example (popular with golf)

indicators.note: mainly means most of it, so the last letter of the city word is dropped

parts.note: Liverpool is an example of a city
in means popular or fashionable
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone keeps bringing up Liverpool, which is popular with golfers.
explanation.definitionFit: Citing is quoting or referring to something, i.e. mentioning it.

clue.text: Top craftsmen perhaps netting theologian's fish

indicators.note: netting means catching in a net, so the craftsmen word holds the theologian inside

parts.note: tilers work on the top of a house, roofing it
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

explanation.surface: Skilled tradesmen catch a clergyman's fish in their net.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiddlers are very small fish, such as minnows or sticklebacks.

clue.text: Lads upset about short day? Nuts

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters go round the short day
upset means knocked over or disordered, so the letters of lads are jumbled

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday

explanation.surface: Boys get annoyed over a brief day, and the speaker says that's crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' makes ALDS, which 'about' wraps round the short day. 'Nuts' looks like an exclamation of scorn but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Almonds are a common kind of nut, here in the plural.

clue.text: Foolishly, she can — accommodating idiot Englishman

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so the rearranged letters hold the idiot word
foolishly suggests something done without sense, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ass is an idiot

explanation.surface: A woman unwisely puts up a fool who turns out to be English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolishly' makes SENACH, which 'accommodating' wraps round the idiot. Sassenach is a Scots word, mildly hostile, for an English person.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassenach is a Scottish term for an English person, from the Gaelic for Saxon.

clue.text: Causes amazement, with no hospital strikes

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the hospital letter is taken away

parts.note: to shock is to cause amazement
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Industrial action without a hospital leaves people astonished.
explanation.definitionFit: To sock someone is to punch them hard, so socks means strikes.

clue.text: Sickened by Auden capriciously adopting parliamentary constituency

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the shuffled letters hold the constituency word
capriciously means on a whim, so the letters of Auden are shuffled

parts.note: a seat is a constituency held by a member of parliament

explanation.surface: Someone is disgusted by the poet Auden whimsically standing for a seat in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capriciously' makes NAUED, which 'adopting' wraps round the constituency. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be nauseated is to feel sick or disgusted, i.e. sickened.

clue.text: Face such consequences in chamber, for example

definitions.meaning: to face the ... is to accept the unpleasant results of one's actions
chamber ... is one example of a kind of musical composition

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition works only with 'face the', from the idiom; the second takes 'chamber' as the kind of music, not a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing the music means bearing consequences, and chamber is a type of music.

clue.text: Puts a limit on bronze device on ship

parts.note: to cap is to put a limit on
tan is a bronze colour, as of suntanned skin

explanation.surface: A rule limits how much bronze can be fitted to a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a revolving drum on a ship used to wind in cable or anchor rope.

clue.text: Waits around for ships to welcome head of government

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the ships word holds the letter inside

parts.note: liners are large passenger ships

indicators.note: head of means the first letter, so only the start of government is used

explanation.surface: Someone hangs about for ocean liners to greet the prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to stay around longer than needed, waiting.

clue.text: 10's on us if remixed

definitions.note: 10 is the music answer, and the apostrophe s stands for is, so the definition is a type of music

indicators.note: remixed means mixed again, as with a recording, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Music is down to us if it gets remixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 10's reads as '10 is', so the definition is a form of MUSIC, the answer to 10.
explanation.definitionFit: Fusion is a musical style blending jazz with rock or other genres.

clue.text: Money lost in selling if car ices over

indicators.note: over suggests the letters are knocked over and rearranged, as when a car overturns on ice

explanation.surface: Cash is lost when you sell if your car is iced over.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrifice in trade is a sale at a loss, the money forgone being lost.

clue.text: Encroach upon resorts in very French surroundings

indicators.note: in tells us the resorts word is put inside the French word
surroundings means the French word encloses the resorts word

parts.note: tres is French for very
spas are health resorts

explanation.surface: Someone intrudes on holiday resorts set in very French surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass is to enter land without right, encroaching on it.

clue.text: How crude shelter carried by sleigh was shifted?

indicators.note: carried by means held within, so the sleigh word holds the shelter word

parts.note: a sled is a sleigh
a hovel is a crude shelter

explanation.surface: A riddle about how a rough hut was moved on a sleigh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How' and 'was' are links: the definition is 'shifted', in the sense of moved with a spade.
explanation.definitionFit: Shovelled means moved earth or snow with a spade, i.e. shifted it.

clue.text: Justifications from French receivers

parts.note: de is French for from
fences are receivers of stolen goods

explanation.surface: Excuses come from some French recipients.
explanation.definitionFit: Defences are arguments justifying one's conduct, i.e. justifications.

clue.text: Greek's old banger in call for help

definitions.note: the apostrophe s stands for is, so the definition is simply a Greek

indicators.note: in tells us the old car word sits inside the distress call

parts.note: SOS is the Morse distress signal
a crate is an old, battered car, a banger in British slang

explanation.surface: A Greek man's old car is stuck and he signals for help.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a ramshackle old car.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates was the Athenian philosopher, a famous ancient Greek.

clue.text: A fine idiomatic expression heard in violent disturbances

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: heard says the expression word is spoken, giving letters that match its sound

parts.note: a phrase is an idiomatic expression

explanation.surface: A neat turn of speech is overheard during a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Affrays are public fights or brawls, legally violent disturbances of the peace.

clue.text: 10 back working after college

indicators.note: after means the reversed piece comes after the college word

parts.note: tech is short for technical college

indicators.note: back means the working word is read backwards

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is

explanation.surface: Music is back on after a college course.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is MUSIC, so the definition is a genre of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Techno is a style of electronic dance music, one form of music.

clue.text: Removed and worked out with no sign of hesitation

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the hesitation letters are cut out

parts.note: exercised means worked out in a gym
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone took it out and exercised without pausing.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise is to cut out, so excised means removed.

clue.text: Leave temporary accommodation to support lower socio-economic groups

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another goes beneath it

parts.note: D and E are the lowest classes in British social grading
a camp is temporary accommodation, such as tents

explanation.surface: Quit a temporary shelter to help the poorer classes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain's social grade system (A, B, C1, C2, D, E), D and E are the lowest groups.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly.

clue.text: 10's light boat plies regularly

definitions.note: the apostrophe s stands for is, so the definition is a type of music

parts.note: a skiff is a light rowing boat

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of plies is taken

explanation.surface: Music played as a light boat goes back and forth regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is MUSIC; skiffle was a 1950s British folk-blues style played on homemade instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiffle is a style of popular music using guitars, washboards and tea-chest basses.

clue.text: Dress down, feeling the chill after the end of mass

indicators.note: after means the chilly word comes after that letter
the end of means only the last letter of mass is used

parts.note: cold means feeling the chill

explanation.surface: A churchgoer gets told off while shivering at the end of Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress down is to reprimand someone, which is what scold means.

clue.text: Fugitive's key — copy key!

definitions.note: the apostrophe s stands for is, so the definition is a fugitive

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
to ape is to copy
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: An escaped prisoner's most important thing is to copy a key.
explanation.walkthrough: The two keys differ: the first is on a keyboard, the second is a musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapee is someone who has escaped, i.e. a fugitive.

clue.text: Old people finding source of coal in mines

indicators.note: in tells us the first letter of coal goes inside the mines word

parts.note: pits are mines

indicators.note: source of means the beginning, the first letter

explanation.surface: Elderly miners find where coal comes from underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland.

clue.text: Approval from Continentals means contacting board

parts.note: oui is French for yes
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: Getting a European yes means getting in touch with the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' is a link; the board is used at seances for contacting spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ouija board is used in seances, supposedly to contact the dead.

clue.text: State student allocated to form 1 is sort of 10

indicators.note: allocated to means the state and student letters are attached after the form

parts.note: a form is a school class
I is the Roman numeral one
CA is California, a US state
L is a learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A state school pupil allocated to the first form is a kind of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical is a broad genre of Western art music, one sort of music.

clue.text: Embellishes the truth of raised hemlines!

definitions.meaning: to dress something up is to make it sound better than it really is
read literally, frocks going up, as when hemlines are raised

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase as plurals of the garment moving upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing up a story means embellishing it; dresses going up means hemlines raised.

clue.text: Drugged, but oddly steady after party

indicators.note: after means the odd letters come after the party word

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters of steady are taken

explanation.surface: Someone drugged, though steady in an odd way after the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosed means given a dose of a drug, i.e. drugged.
